prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM System. Airports: Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport (own authority). Modes: Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, Slot Compliance State. System: Regional Flow Platform alias Cedarbell (coordination only). Parts: Demand Prediction Service alias Marlinstone, Capacity Assessment Module (CAM), Slot Allocation Engine (feasibility only), Airport CDM Portal, Digital Briefing Room, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console (both only under accountable roles), Contingency Operations Console, Weather Ingest Gateway alias Orchard, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter, Alert Distribution Hub, Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service, Collaborative Decision Log, North/South Runway Meter, East/West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector, Common Situation Display. Actors: Regional Flow Manager alias Copperfin (owns intent; reviews Airport Capacity Plan, Ground Delay Program, Tactical Regulation Proposal; authorizes measures; confirms airline recovery priorities before revised constraints published); Airline Operations Coordinator alias Saffron; Slot Coordinator (reviews priority requests vs equity/feasibility during GDP); Meteorology Briefing Officer (Storm Cell Snapshot, weather triggers, overrides); Airport Duty Manager; Tower Supervisor (Runway Inspection Note); Ground Handling Dispatcher (sends Crew Bus Delay Slip); Handling Resource Planner (correlates handling impacts); also Airspace Sector Planner, Aircraft Operator Representative, Network Operations Liaison, Ramp Control Lead, Deicing Coordinator, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator (mandatory safety escalation), Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer. Flows: airlines→Flight Intent Message (route, timing, registration, turnaround, crew, connections)→Airline Interface Adapter (Identity Access Service account; validates, maps codes via Business Rules Registry; rejects invalid with machine-readable reasons)→Flight Data Exchange→Marlinstone→demand by time band; accepted intents shown proposed on Common Situation Display until Cedarbell reconciles; changes only via updated Flight Intent Message. Sector Load Monitor→airspace demand. Orchard validates weather (Time Synchronization Service); bad feeds marked degraded, not excluded→CAM (uses Airport Capacity Plan, Airport Acceptance Rate, Storm Cell Snapshot)→limits, GDP test; Runway Meters; Apron Sensors→Ramp Movement Board. Slot Allocation

Document units:
S142: The Ramp Control Lead uses the Ramp Movement Board to identify whether the proposed recovery action can be supported without creating surface congestion.
S143: The Tower Supervisor reviews metering effects in the Tower Sequence Manager when airline recovery actions change the expected departure order.
S144: The Airport Duty Manager monitors the Common Situation Display to ensure airline recovery decisions remain consistent with terminal capacity and passenger processing conditions.
S145: Disputed constraints are captured in the Collaborative Decision Log with the requesting airline, operational rationale, decision owner, and final resolution.
S146: During Adverse Weather Mode or a Capacity Reduction State, airline operations centres are expected to submit conservative intents that distinguish firm operating plans from speculative recovery options.
S147: During the Recovery Phase, the Regional Flow Platform permits more frequent intent updates while retaining the previous values needed for audit and performance review.
S148: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares submitted intents, issued constraints, actual off-block times, and achieved arrival outcomes to improve recovery playbooks.
S149: All airline integration transactions are time-stamped by the Time Synchronization Service and preserved in the Audit Event Ledger for post-operations reconstruction.
S150: The Airport CDM Portal provides the shared operational workspace where airport participants maintain a common view of departure readiness, arrival constraints, surface conditions, and slot impacts.
S151: For local voice coordination, the Airport CDM Portal is also known as Foxglove.
S152: Access to the Airport CDM Portal is controlled by the Identity Access Service so that each user sees only the workspaces, aircraft, stands, and decision records appropriate to the assigned role.
S153: The primary workspace presents the Common Situation Display with synchronized clocks, active operating state, airport demand, runway configuration, stand occupancy, and milestone status for each managed movement.
S154: The departure workspace is centered on Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, boarding readiness, aircraft servicing progress, and pushback coordination status.
S155: The arrival workspace shows expected landing demand, stand allocation risk, inbound regulation effects, and handling readiness indicators needed to protect the Airport Acceptance Rate.
S156: A dedicated milestone view records the planned, target, estimated, actual, and manually confirmed times for each turnaround event that affects a regulated departure or constrained arrival.
S157: The Airline Operations Coordinator is responsible for keeping the Flight Intent Message status, Target Off Block Time, passenger readiness indicator, and aircraft operational constraint notes current for each represented flight.
